correctness.finding: PASS. The threshold-image proof is sound. For t>eta_n the high-weight image A_t is finite with fewer than n points; separating those image points and cutting off the fibers at a slightly higher level gives a rank-<n operator R with ||T-R|| arbitrarily close to t. For t<eta_n, n separated peak functions produce an isometric l_infinity^n on which T is bounded below by t, giving the matching approximation, Bernstein, and Gelfand lower bounds. Composing with evaluation at the selected preimages reduces the Kolmogorov lower bound to a diagonal map whose image contains t times the l_infinity^n unit ball. Below rho, infinitely many distinct high-weight image points yield disjoint peak functions spanning an isometric c0 on which T is bounded below, which forces the same lower distance against compact, weakly compact, finitely strictly singular, and strictly singular ideals. The finite-rank upper approximants give the reverse distance bound.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Takagi–Miura–Takahasi determine the essential norm of weighted composition operators on C(X) from the same kind of threshold image, so the compact-distance component is prior art. Classical compactness/weak-compactness and compact disjointness-preserver structure are also prior. The audited contribution is the exact all-index identity a_n=b_n=c_n=d_n=eta_n together with the common distances to weakly compact/FSS/SS ideals and quantitative c0 witnesses. Targeted searches for approximation/Bernstein/Gelfand/Kolmogorov profiles of weighted composition operators on C(K) found no covering theorem; the closest surfaced s-number literature concerns other function spaces. Broad older disjointness-preserver literature remains a residual priority risk, so no novelty is assigned beyond this exact profile.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. A single explicit rearrangement of fiber-maximal weights simultaneously determines four classical s-number scales and several operator-ideal distances. The c0 witness also explains structurally why compactness, weak compactness, finite strict singularity, and strict singularity collapse for this operator class. This is a useful quantitative refinement of the known essential-norm threshold theorem.
